title: Doppler effect; Expanding universe and cosmology
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: A03-2#t3 term and clue written for the game; A03-2#t2 term and clue written for the game; W11-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W11-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: A03-2#N.3, W11-1#N.9, A03-2#N.7, W11-1#N.6, A03-2#N.8, W11-1#N.13a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Recession speed
items.clue: How fast a galaxy is moving away from us, found from its red shift.

items.label: Hubble's law
items.clue: Finding that a distant galaxy twice as far away is moving away twice as fast.

items.label: Doppler effect
items.clue: Shift in observed pitch when a source moves: higher when approaching, lower when receding.

items.label: Wavefront
items.clue: Surface sent out by a source at a steady rate; bunched ahead when the source moves, spread out behind.

questions.stem: A galaxy at a distance of 1.2 × 10²⁴ m recedes from the Earth at 2800 km s⁻¹. What value of the Hubble constant does this give?
questions.explanation: H₀ = speed ÷ distance = 2.8 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ ÷ 1.2 × 10²⁴ m = 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹.

questions.stem: Predict first. Every absorption line in the spectrum of a star in our galaxy is at a slightly longer wavelength than the same line measured in the laboratory. What does this show about the star?

options.text: It is a cool, red-looking star.
It is moving away from Earth.
It is a very long way from Earth.

questions.stem: A measured value of the Hubble constant is 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹. What is the estimated age of the universe? (1 year = 3.16 × 10⁷ s)

A spectral line of hydrogen has a wavelength of 656.3 nm when measured in the laboratory. A galaxy is moving directly away from Earth at 3.00 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. At what wavelength is this line observed in the spectrum of the galaxy?

Galaxy P is 2.0 × 10²⁴ m away and recedes at 5.2 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Galaxy Q is 6.0 × 10²⁴ m away and recedes at 1.56 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Assuming each has always moved at its present speed, how long ago was each at our position? (1 year = 3.16 × 10⁷ s)

options.text: P 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years ago, Q 3.7 × 10¹⁰ years ago: they set off at different times.
Both 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years ago: they were together then, at a common start.
Both 3.8 × 10¹⁷ years ago: they were together then, at a common start.
Never: the further galaxy moves faster, so the two can never have been together.

questions.explanation: Distance ÷ speed = 3.8 × 10¹⁷ s for both, which is 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years. Speed ∝ distance gives every galaxy the same time.

questions.stem: A calcium absorption line has a wavelength of 393.4 nm in the laboratory. In the spectrum of a distant galaxy the same line is at 401.3 nm. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the galaxy's velocity relative to Earth?
questions.explanation: Δλ = 7.9 nm; v = c × 7.9/393.4 = 6.0 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Longer wavelength → receding.
